MEMO
To: All Warehouse Staff
From: Dana Ortiz, Operations Manager
Re: New Forklift Check Procedure

Starting Monday, March 3, every forklift must be inspected at the start of each shift, not once a week as before. Drivers will use the new checklist posted at the charging station. The checklist covers brakes, horn, lights, tires, and fluid levels. If any item fails, the driver must tag the forklift "Out of Service" and tell a supervisor before using another machine. Completed checklists go in the gray box by the time clock. We are making this change because two forklifts had brake problems last month that a daily check would have caught. Thank you for helping keep everyone safe.

According to the memo, how often must each forklift now be inspected?
choices: Once a week
At the start of every shift
Only when a supervisor asks
At the end of every month
oneLineConcept: Stated details: find the exact line in the text
explanation:
The memo says every forklift "must be inspected at the start of each shift, not once a week as before." This is a stated detail, so the answer comes straight from the text.

**Wrong choices**
- "Once a week": "Once a week" was the old rule. The memo says this is being replaced.
- "Only when a supervisor asks": The memo makes the check a regular duty for every shift, not something done only on request.
- "At the end of every month": The memo never mentions a monthly inspection.

Most adults need seven or more hours of sleep each night, yet many get far less. Researchers have found that short sleep affects more than mood. During deep sleep, the body releases hormones that repair muscles and help control appetite. When sleep is cut short, levels of a hormone that signals hunger tend to rise, while a hormone that signals fullness tends to fall. This may explain why tired people often reach for snacks. Sleep also gives the brain time to sort and store new memories, so people who sleep poorly may have trouble learning new tasks. Simple habits can help: going to bed at the same time each night, keeping the bedroom dark and cool, and putting screens away an hour before bed.

Which sentence best states the main idea of the passage?
choices: Most adults sleep more than seven hours a night.
Getting enough sleep matters for the body and the brain in several ways.
Bedrooms should be kept dark and cool.
Tired people often reach for snacks.
oneLineConcept: Main idea: the point that covers the whole passage
explanation:
The passage explains how sleep affects hormones, appetite, muscle repair, and memory, and then gives tips for better sleep. The only choice that covers all of this is that enough sleep matters for both body and brain.

**Wrong choices**
- "Most adults sleep more than seven hours a night.": The passage says many adults get far less than seven hours, the opposite of this choice.
- "Bedrooms should be kept dark and cool.": Keeping the bedroom dark and cool is one tip near the end; it is a detail.
- "Tired people often reach for snacks.": Snacking is one example in the passage, not the main point.

choices: Feeling hungrier than usual
Faster repair of tired muscles
Needing fewer snacks during the day
Learning new tasks more quickly
oneLineConcept: Inference: apply what the passage says to a new case

- "Faster repair of tired muscles": Muscle repair happens during deep sleep, so short sleep would not make it faster.
- "Needing fewer snacks during the day": The passage says tired people often reach for more snacks, not fewer.
- "Learning new tasks more quickly": The passage says poor sleep may make learning new tasks harder, not easier.

Riverside Public Library: Changes to Borrowing Rules

Beginning June 1, the library will no longer charge late fees on books, movies, or music. Our staff found that fines kept many families, especially those with young children, from coming back after a single overdue book. Items that are more than 30 days overdue will still be marked as lost, and the borrower will be asked to return them or pay to replace them before checking out anything new. The borrowing limit will rise from 25 to 40 items per card. Laptops and Wi-Fi hotspots are not part of this change; they must still be returned within 7 days, and a $5 daily fee still applies.

According to the notice, which items will still have a daily late fee?
choices: Laptops and Wi-Fi hotspots
Books and magazines
Children's picture books
Movies and music
oneLineConcept: Exceptions: watch for 'not part of this change'
explanation:
The notice ends with an exception: laptops and Wi-Fi hotspots "are not part of this change" and a $5 daily fee still applies to them.

**Wrong choices**
- "Books and magazines": The notice says books will no longer have late fees.
- "Children's picture books": Children's books are books, so they have no late fee under the new rule.
- "Movies and music": Movies and music are named among the items with no more late fees.

In the early 1930s, a long drought struck the southern Great Plains. For years before, farmers had plowed up millions of acres of native grass to plant wheat. The deep roots of that grass had held the soil in place. When the rains stopped and the crops died, there was nothing to keep the dry topsoil from blowing away. Huge dust storms, some stretching hundreds of miles, rolled across Kansas, Oklahoma, and Texas. Families sealed their windows with wet sheets, yet dust still covered their tables. Many people lost their farms and moved west in search of work. In response, the federal government created programs that paid farmers to plant trees as windbreaks and to use methods that kept soil from washing or blowing away.

According to the passage, what had held the soil in place before farmers plowed the land?
choices: Rows of trees planted as windbreaks
The deep roots of native grass
Rows of wheat
Heavy rainfall every spring
oneLineConcept: Stated detail: scan for the key words in the question
explanation:
The passage says, "The deep roots of that grass had held the soil in place." "That grass" refers to the native grass farmers had plowed up.

**Wrong choices**
- "Rows of trees planted as windbreaks": Tree windbreaks came later, as part of the government's response.
- "Rows of wheat": Wheat replaced the grass; when the wheat died, nothing held the soil.
- "Heavy rainfall every spring": The passage mentions a drought but never says spring rain held the soil.

Drought began, then trees were planted, then grass was plowed up.
Families moved west, then grass was plowed up, then dust storms spread.

oneLineConcept: Sequence: put events in the order the text gives

- "Families moved west, then grass was plowed up, then dust storms spread.": Families moved west because of the storms, so that came later.
- "Dust storms spread, then grass was plowed up, then drought began.": The storms came after the grass was gone, not before it was plowed.

Many homeowners ask whether rooftop solar panels make sense for them. The answer depends on three things. First, the roof must get strong sunlight for most of the day; a roof shaded by tall trees or buildings will produce much less power. Second, the roof should be in good shape. Panels usually last 25 years or more, so replacing an old roof first can avoid the cost of removing and reinstalling the panels later. Third, owners should look at local electricity prices and any state programs that lower the cost of installation. Where power is expensive and programs are generous, panels may pay for themselves sooner. Where power is cheap, it can take much longer to make back the money.

What is the main purpose of the passage?
choices: To describe how solar panels turn sunlight into power
To explain what to consider before getting rooftop solar panels
To argue that every home should have solar panels
To warn readers that solar panels damage roofs
oneLineConcept: Main idea of an informational text: what it mostly does
explanation:
The passage opens with the question of whether solar panels make sense and then lists three things to consider: sunlight, roof condition, and local prices and programs. Its main purpose is to explain those factors.

**Wrong choices**
- "To describe how solar panels turn sunlight into power": The passage never explains how panels make electricity.
- "To argue that every home should have solar panels": The passage says "the answer depends," so it does not claim every home should have panels.
- "To warn readers that solar panels damage roofs": The passage says to fix an old roof first to avoid moving panels later, not that panels damage roofs.

Job Posting: Part-Time Maintenance Assistant, Greenway Apartments

Hours: 20 hours per week, Tuesday through Friday mornings, with one Saturday a month.
Pay: $19 per hour.
Duties: Replace light bulbs and air filters, clean common areas, help with simple repairs such as fixing leaky faucets, and keep a log of completed work orders.
Requirements: A valid driver's license and the ability to lift 50 pounds. Basic hand-tool skills are required; plumbing or electrical experience is helpful but not required.
To apply: Email a short letter and a list of past jobs to the office manager by April 15. Applicants chosen for an interview will be called within one week after the deadline.

Which of the following is a requirement for the job?
choices: The ability to lift 50 pounds
Electrical experience
Weekend work every week
Plumbing experience
oneLineConcept: Required vs. helpful: read qualifiers carefully
explanation:
Under "Requirements," the posting lists a valid driver's license, the ability to lift 50 pounds, and basic hand-tool skills.

**Wrong choices**
- "Electrical experience": Electrical experience is also listed as helpful but not required.
- "Weekend work every week": The job includes only one Saturday a month, not every weekend.
- "Plumbing experience": The posting says plumbing experience is "helpful but not required."

By about April 17

- "By about May 15": May 15 is a month after the deadline, far longer than one week.

When the United States was founded, most states allowed only white men who owned property to vote. Over the next two centuries, the right to vote grew through a series of changes to the Constitution. The Fifteenth Amendment, ratified in 1870, said a citizen's right to vote could not be denied because of race. In practice, however, many states used poll taxes and literacy tests to keep Black citizens from voting. The Nineteenth Amendment, ratified in 1920, barred denying the vote because of sex. The Twenty-fourth Amendment, ratified in 1964, banned poll taxes in federal elections, and the Voting Rights Act of 1965 outlawed literacy tests. In 1971, the Twenty-sixth Amendment lowered the voting age to 18.

According to the passage, what did the Twenty-sixth Amendment do?
choices: It outlawed literacy tests.
It banned poll taxes in federal elections.
It barred denying the vote because of sex.
It lowered the voting age to 18.
oneLineConcept: Matching details: names and dates go together
explanation:
The last sentence says that in 1971 the Twenty-sixth Amendment lowered the voting age to 18.

**Wrong choices**
- "It outlawed literacy tests.": Literacy tests were outlawed by the Voting Rights Act of 1965, which was a law, not an amendment.
- "It banned poll taxes in federal elections.": Banning poll taxes in federal elections was the Twenty-fourth Amendment.
- "It barred denying the vote because of sex.": Barring denial because of sex was the Nineteenth Amendment.

- "It was the first amendment about voting rights to be ratified.": "However" signals a contrast, not an order. The passage says nothing about earlier voting amendments.
- "It was quickly repealed by Congress.": The passage never says the amendment was repealed.

Food Safety Tips for Home Cooks

Bacteria grow fastest between 40°F and 140°F, a range often called the danger zone. To keep food safe, refrigerate leftovers within two hours of cooking, or within one hour if the room is hotter than 90°F. Thaw frozen meat in the refrigerator, in cold water that is changed every 30 minutes, or in the microwave, but never on the counter. Use a food thermometer instead of guessing: poultry is safe at 165°F, and ground beef at 160°F. Finally, keep raw meat away from ready-to-eat foods such as salad, and wash cutting boards with hot, soapy water after each use.

According to the tips, which method of thawing meat should never be used?
choices: Leaving it on the counter
Thawing it in the microwave
Thawing it in cold water changed every 30 minutes
Thawing it in the refrigerator
oneLineConcept: Look for strong words like 'never' and 'always'
explanation:
The passage lists three safe ways to thaw meat and then says, "but never on the counter."

**Wrong choices**
- "Thawing it in the microwave": The microwave is one of the safe methods listed.
- "Thawing it in cold water changed every 30 minutes": Cold water changed every 30 minutes is one of the safe methods listed.
- "Thawing it in the refrigerator": The refrigerator is one of the safe methods listed.

oneLineConcept: Implied reasons: connect advice to the details around it

In 1869, engineer John A. Roebling designed a bridge to connect Brooklyn and Manhattan across the East River. Before construction began, his foot was crushed in an accident at the dock, and he died weeks later. His son, Washington Roebling, took over. While working in the deep underwater chambers used to build the towers' foundations, Washington developed decompression sickness, which left him too ill to visit the site. Watching through a telescope from his apartment, he passed instructions to the crews through his wife, Emily Warren Roebling. Emily studied engineering, met with officials, and handled daily questions for years. When the Brooklyn Bridge opened in 1883, she was the first person to cross it.

Which statement best describes Emily Warren Roebling's role, based on the passage?
choices: She was a city official who approved the project.
She was a key link between her husband and the builders.
She worked in the underwater chambers.
She designed the original plan for the bridge.
oneLineConcept: Roles of people: infer from what they did
explanation:
The passage says Washington passed instructions to the crews through Emily, and that she studied engineering, met with officials, and handled daily questions. She connected him to the work.

**Wrong choices**
- "She was a city official who approved the project.": Emily met with officials; she was not one herself.
- "She worked in the underwater chambers.": Washington, not Emily, worked in the underwater chambers.
- "She designed the original plan for the bridge.": John A. Roebling designed the bridge.

Community Recycling Update

Starting in September, the city will switch to single-stream recycling. Residents will no longer need to sort paper, plastic, and metal into separate bins; all clean recyclables can go into one blue cart. Glass, however, must still go to one of the four drop-off centers, because broken glass damages the sorting machines. Plastic bags should not go in the cart. They wrap around the machines' moving parts and force workers to stop the line to cut them free. Please return plastic bags to grocery stores that collect them. Food-covered items such as greasy pizza boxes belong in the trash, since food spoils the paper they are mixed with.

Under the new system, where should residents put clean cans, paper, and plastic bottles?
choices: In the trash
Together in one blue cart
In three separate bins
At a glass drop-off center
oneLineConcept: Stated detail: the main change in a notice
explanation:
The notice says residents "will no longer need to sort paper, plastic, and metal into separate bins; all clean recyclables can go into one blue cart."

**Wrong choices**
- "In the trash": Clean recyclables go in the blue cart; only food-covered items go in the trash.
- "In three separate bins": Separate bins were the old system that the city is replacing.
- "At a glass drop-off center": Drop-off centers are only for glass.

Scientists cannot yet predict the exact day a volcano will erupt, but they can often tell when one is becoming restless. As melted rock, called magma, rises underground, it pushes the ground upward. Instruments that measure tiny changes in the ground's height can detect this swelling. Rising magma also cracks surrounding rock, creating swarms of small earthquakes that sensors pick up. In addition, gases such as sulfur dioxide escape through vents before an eruption, and an increase in these gases can be measured from the ground or from aircraft. When several of these warning signs appear together, officials may order people living nearby to leave.

According to the passage, what causes swarms of small earthquakes before an eruption?
choices: Aircraft flying over the volcano
Instruments measuring the ground
Gases escaping through vents
Rising magma cracking the surrounding rock
oneLineConcept: Cause and effect inside a science text
explanation:
The passage says, "Rising magma also cracks surrounding rock, creating swarms of small earthquakes."

**Wrong choices**
- "Aircraft flying over the volcano": Aircraft are used to measure gases, not cause earthquakes.
- "Instruments measuring the ground": Instruments only detect changes; they do not cause them.
- "Gases escaping through vents": Escaping gases are a separate warning sign; the passage does not say they cause earthquakes.

Letter to the Editor

Last spring, a group of neighbors turned the empty lot on Fifth Street into a community garden. The city let us use the land for free, and a local hardware store donated tools. Today, thirty families grow vegetables there, and we give extra produce to the food pantry every Saturday. Children from the elementary school across the street visit once a week to learn how seeds grow. Now the city plans to sell the lot to a developer. I urge the city council to keep the garden open. It feeds families, teaches children, and brings neighbors together in a way an empty building site never could.

What is the writer's main purpose in this letter?
choices: To announce that the lot has been sold
To thank the hardware store for donating tools
To explain how to start a community garden
To persuade the city council to keep the garden open
oneLineConcept: Purpose: look for what the writer asks readers to do
explanation:
After describing the garden's benefits, the writer says, "I urge the city council to keep the garden open." The details about families, children, and the food pantry support that request.

**Wrong choices**
- "To announce that the lot has been sold": The city only "plans to sell" the lot; it has not been sold.
- "To thank the hardware store for donating tools": The donation is one detail in the letter's history of the garden, not its purpose.
- "To explain how to start a community garden": The letter does not give steps for starting a garden.
